description:
Recovery finds the tag-0 materializer by ROLL CALL: locking_phase.ex:161-164 locks every advertised materializer in the cluster ({_service_id, {:materializer, _location}} -> true, unconditional — logs by contrast are filtered to the old layout's log set), then asks each its shard_id and runs a most-advanced-durable contest to pick tag 0. That is a discovery pass where FDB has a lookup.

FDB's chain: coordinators -> cstate (DBCoreState) -> old tlog set -> peek txnStateTag -> txnStateStore -> keyServers/serverKeys/config. The location of the metadata store is recorded OUT OF BAND; the metadata itself stays in the replicated store. Recovery reads nothing from storage servers at all.

Bedrock's metadata lives in the keyspace, served by the tag-0 materializer, so we cannot copy FDB's answer (relocate metadata into a log-replayed side store) without abandoning 'the keyspace is the channel'. We CAN copy its SHAPE: record where the metadata lives out of band, one indirection, and keep the metadata in the keyspace.

CHANGE: add system_materializers (tag 0's member set) to CoreState and its backing ClusterBootstrap schema, next to logs. Recovery then locks exactly the named members instead of the whole cluster's materializers.

WHY IT IS BOUNDED: the TSL docstring forbids anything O(workers) in the broadcast. Tag 0's member set is O(replication factor) — the same order as logs, which already rides there. The rule exists to keep the shard->materializer map (O(shards x replicas)) out; tag 0 alone does not violate it. Note the family is set-valued as of bedrock-q67.21.9, so this is a member SET, not a single ref.

KILLS A REAL HAZARD: on the EXISTING-cluster path, find_or_create_materializer (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:329-343) CREATES A FRESH EMPTY tag-0 materializer when no advertised materializer claims tag 0, then reads the shard layout from it. The trigger is mundane — the node hosting tag 0 has not re-registered when recovery runs. RecoveryCapabilityTracker is only a change-detection hash, not a precondition, so nothing gates it. fresh_cluster?/1 is NOT the bug (it correctly keys off the old TSL's logs); the invent path is.

FDB is unambiguous here: it refuses to recover without a quorum of its cstate-named tlogs. Recovery must never fabricate the metadata store. With tag-0 members in CoreState, 'named but unavailable' becomes an explicit stall-and-retry and the invent path stops existing.

SPIKE FIRST (decides whether this is a bug fix or only a simplification): a freshly created tag-0 materializer is unlocked at recovery_version (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:212-238). Determine whether such an impostor can therefore report a durable version at or above the real tag-0 worker's and WIN the most-advanced-durable contest on a subsequent recovery — permanently shadowing the real metadata. Prove or refute with a falsifiable spike before writing the fix; if it can win, this is P1, not P2.

DUAL RECORDING IS INTENDED: tag 0 stays in the materializers/ keyspace family too — commit proxies need routing for \xFF reads. CoreState is authoritative for BOOTSTRAP, the keyspace for ROUTING, and recovery writes both in the same recovery. FDB does the same with tlogs (cstate + logSystemConfig).

TAG-0 MEMBERSHIP IS RECOVERY-ONLY: the distributor never manages tag 0, matching FDB where changing the tlog set is a recovery-accompanied operation. That keeps CoreState from needing a second writer, and draws the line bedrock-q67.21.13 depends on.

DEPENDS ON: bedrock-q67.21.11 (CoreState must exist to add a field to it).
title: Tag-0 materializer members ride CoreState; recovery stops inventing the metadata store
